Despite previous unsuccessful attempts to change state law, Tesla’s legal victory now allows direct sales in Arizona, a move opposed by the Arizona Automobile Dealers Association.

summary: The article discusses why Tesla does not participate in J.D. Power's annual Initial Quality Study. Tesla does not allow J.D. Power access to its customer registration data, which is necessary for the survey, despite other automakers cooperating. J.D. Power acknowledges Tesla's quality but notes their non-participation prevents inclusion in the industry benchmark study.

title: Cummins to Offer Option of Electric Engines by 2019
summary: Cummins Inc. plans to have a fully electrified powertrain system available for commercial customers by 2019 and a range-extended electric truck ready in 2020. The company is actively developing its next-generation heavy-duty diesel engine and sees electrification as a critical area for innovation, especially for urban pickup-and-delivery operations. Analysts view Cummins' move into electric powertrains as a significant step to address potential long-term risks from electric technology replacing diesel.

title: Tesla, Inc. Starts Selling Tesla-Branded Solar Panels in Its Stores
summary: Tesla, Inc. has begun selling its newly launched Tesla-branded solar panels in its stores, following a successful pilot program. This move signifies the company's full integration of solar products into its brand after the SolarCity acquisition and aims to leverage Tesla's retail footprint for sales and cost synergies. The company anticipates energy product sales to become a larger share of its revenue.

title: States Betting on Giant Batteries to Cut Carbon
summary: Several U.S. states and electric power companies are increasingly adopting giant batteries to store electricity from renewable sources like wind and solar, aiming to reduce carbon emissions. States like New York, Nevada, and Maryland are creating energy storage targets or incentives, following California, Oregon, and Massachusetts which have mandates. This trend helps address the intermittency of renewable energy, allows for greater use of renewables during peak demand, and contributes to replacing or supplementing fossil fuel power plants.

title: Elon Musk Teases Sunday Announcement About Tesla Model 3 Timing
summary: Elon Musk announced via Twitter that an update on the Tesla Model 3 timing would be provided on Sunday. The Model 3, priced at $35,000, is set to begin production next month. This anticipation has significantly boosted Tesla's shares, elevating its market capitalization above competitors like General Motors Co. and Ford Motor Co.

title: Model 3 launch could signal the beginning -- or end -- for Tesla
summary: The launch of Tesla's Model 3 is a pivotal moment for the company, signaling a move from niche luxury carmaker to a mass-market electric vehicle provider. While Tesla has surprised some by starting production on time, the company faces immense pressure to meet ambitious production targets and overcome challenges in distribution and service infrastructure. Analysts have varying expectations for Tesla's ability to scale production and maintain customer satisfaction, especially given past issues with other models and the high expectations set by Elon Musk.

title: Musk Tweets Pictures of First Model 3 to Roll Off the Line
summary: Elon Musk tweeted pictures of the first Tesla Model 3 sedan to roll off the assembly line. The car was a gift from board member Ira Ehrenpreis for Musk's 46th birthday. Tesla anticipates exponential production increases for the Model 3, despite recent concerns about weakening demand for its Model S and a drop in registrations in key markets like California and Hong Kong.

title: Southern Company launches Tesla Powerpack demo project
summary: Southern Company and its Gulf Power subsidiary have initiated a two-year research project in Florida using a Tesla Powerpack to better understand the operational aspects of commercial and industrial energy storage systems. The project, in collaboration with the Electric Power Research Institute and Tesla, aims to evaluate the benefits of storage for services like peak shaving, demand management, and backup power. This marks Southern Company's first Tesla Powerpack project and Gulf Power's first storage project, signaling a potentially significant step in energy storage for a major utility operating beyond high-penetration renewable energy areas.

title: 888 Boylston Takes Sustainability to New Level for Boston Properties
summary: Boston Properties' 888 Boylston Street building has become Boston's most sustainable building, featuring innovative designs like wind turbines and a chilled beam system. This project builds on the company's prior sustainability milestones and serves as a "living laboratory" for green design, educating both the public and the industry.

title: A more nimble GM is willing to drop struggling markets and cars
summary: General Motors under CEO Mary Barra is aggressively focusing on profitability by prioritizing high-selling models like crossovers, SUVs, and pickups, and exiting struggling markets to prepare for a future dominated by self-driving vehicles. This strategy, though not yet boosting the stock price significantly, involves considering the elimination of several historically notable car models and has already led to the sale of its European division and exits from India and South Africa operations. GM is making significant cost cuts and investing in future technologies like self-driving cars, ride-hailing, and ride-sharing services.

title: Edison CEO Applauds New SoCal Electric Bus Manufacturing Plant
summary: Edison International President and CEO Pedro Pizarro applauded the opening of Proterra's new electric bus manufacturing plant in the City of Industry, California, alongside Governor Jerry Brown. The facility is expected to create 150 new jobs and produce up to four electric buses per week. Southern California Edison, a subsidiary of Edison International, will partner with Proterra and Foothill Transit to provide charging infrastructure for the new electric buses as part of its plan to expand electric transportation and reduce greenhouse gas emissions.

title: Over-the-air software updates coming to GM cars and trucks
summary: General Motors announced plans to introduce a new electrical vehicle architecture and infotainment system capable of over-the-air (OTA) updates before 2020. This move will bring GM closer to competitors like Tesla, which has been utilizing OTA updates for years, and is expected to save automakers billions and alter their relationship with drivers and dealerships. GM also recently hired a chief data officer to strengthen data analytics for customer experience and business-to-business opportunities.

title: Tesla’s Big Reveal Shows a Rough Road Ahead
summary: Tesla unveiled its Model 3 sedan, with CEO Elon Musk delivering the first 30 vehicles. While the company holds over 500,000 refundable deposits, investors are cautioned against expecting a similar stock market reaction. The article suggests that despite the fanfare, the Model 3 might struggle to meet the mass-market hype surrounding it.

title: Tesla, Inc.'s Model 3: What We Know So Far
summary: Ahead of its final unveiling, Tesla had already revealed significant details about the Model 3, including its $35,000 starting price, over 215 miles of range, and sub-six-second 0-60 mph acceleration. The vehicle, smaller than the Model S, features a 15-inch display and will utilize Autopilot sensors, though Supercharging will not be free. Investors were watching closely for additional information at the launch event.

title: Tesla delivers first lower-cost Model 3 cars
summary: Tesla Inc. has delivered its first 30 Model 3 electric cars to employees, marking the release of its long-anticipated affordable vehicle with a $35,000 starting price and 220-mile range. CEO Elon Musk expects "manufacturing hell" for at least six months to meet the goal of producing 500,000 cars next year, with 500,000 people already having placed deposits. The Model 3 aims to transition Tesla from a luxury brand to the mainstream, despite potential production challenges and a global market shift towards SUVs.

title: Industry Focus: Manufacturing
summary: This article discusses the growth spurt in Nevada's manufacturing industry, highlighting challenges and opportunities identified by industry leaders. Key issues include workforce shortages due to rapid expansion and competition from large companies like Tesla and Panasonic, as well as regulatory hurdles. Automation is presented as a significant factor in increasing efficiency and enabling companies to remain competitive in the US.

title: Tesla 3 official launch depends on suppliers
summary: Tesla's ambitious Model 3 launch timeline is heavily reliant on its suppliers' ability to meet high production demands, with CEO Elon Musk stating the company needs to produce 10,000 cars per week. The article highlights the critical role of strong supplier relationships for manufacturers with tight deadlines, citing issues faced by Apple due to supply chain delays. Despite past production struggles and what Musk calls "manufacturing hell," Tesla's proximity to suppliers in Fremont, California, is expected to help them achieve their Model 3 production goals.

title: Tesla to Sell $1.5 Billion in Debt to Fuel Aggressive Expansion
summary: Tesla Inc. is planning to sell $1.5 billion in its first-ever traditional bond offering to finance its aggressive expansion, particularly with the launch of its lower-priced Model 3 sedan. This move signifies the company's shift from a luxury car manufacturer to a mass-market competitor. The bonds are expected to be sold as early as Friday, with Goldman Sachs Group Inc. underwriting the deal.

title: Exclusive: Tesla developing self-driving tech for semi-truck, wants to test in Nevada
summary: Tesla Inc. is developing a self-driving, long-haul electric semi-truck capable of platooning and is seeking to test prototypes in Nevada and California, as revealed through correspondence with the Nevada DMV. This initiative places Tesla in a competitive realm of commercial transport, alongside companies like Uber and Alphabet's Waymo, despite skepticism regarding the economic feasibility of long-haul electric trucking due to battery range limitations. Tesla has been a leader in developing self-driving technology for its luxury cars, including the lower-priced Model 3.

title: Tesla's first junk bond offering is a hit, but now Elon Musk must deliver: 'No more room for excuses'
summary: Tesla successfully raised $1.8 billion, $300 million more than planned, in its first high-yield junk bond offering, indicating strong demand despite a recent drop in high-yield bonds. The company must now deliver on profitability, particularly with its new Model 3, as it has burned through billions of dollars in recent years. Analysts believe this offering shows investor confidence in Tesla's long-term growth story, but emphasize the need for results.

title: Bond investors give Tesla a $1.8 billion endorsement
summary: Bond investors backed Tesla Inc.'s first foray into the U.S. junk bond market, providing a $1.8 billion boost for the electric car maker. The strong demand allowed Tesla to increase its offering from an initial $1.5 billion, with the proceeds intended to finance production of the mass-market Model 3. This successful debt issuance highlights robust investor appetite in the high-yield market, despite some analysts considering it pricey.

title: Merck CEO Resigns from Trump Council after Charlottesville
summary: Merck CEO Kenneth Frazier resigned from President Trump's American Manufacturing Council, citing intolerance and extremism after the Charlottesville violence. Frazier stated his responsibility to take a stand against hatred and bigotry, which prompted a response from Trump regarding drug prices. Other executives, including Elon Musk and Robert Iger, had previously left advisory councils due to disagreements with Trump's policies.

title: Why the Texas lawyer who started Southwest Airlines in 1967 never gave himself a raise or a bonus
summary: Herb Kelleher, co-founder of Southwest Airlines, famously never took a pay raise or bonus to set a good example for employees, instead receiving compensation in stock options. He maintained that this decision aligned with his philosophy of fiscal conservatism for the airline. Kelleher's approach is mirrored by other prominent CEOs like Elon Musk and Mark Zuckerberg, who also take minimal or no salaries.

title: Three CEOs Leave Trump Panel in Protest After Weekend Violence
summary: The CEOs of Intel, Merck & Co., and Under Armour resigned from President Donald Trump's American Manufacturing Council following his initial tepid response to violence at a white supremacist rally in Charlottesville, Virginia. These executives cited the need to take a stand against intolerance and extremism, with Trump responding critically to Merck's CEO Ken Frazier via Twitter. Their resignations follow similar actions by other executives protesting Trump's policies.
source: VOA - Voice of America English News
source_domain: VOA - Voice of America English News

title: SCE’s Wind Energy, Energy Storage Featured in CNBC World TV Show
summary: Southern California Edison's (SCE) leadership in clean energy, particularly its use of wind power and battery storage, was featured in a CNBC World TV series episode titled "Wind." The episode highlighted SCE's Mira Loma battery storage facility, which uses 396 Tesla Powerpacks to store energy, and its connection to the Tehachapi Renewable Transmission Project. Edison International's president and CEO, Pedro Pizarro, also discussed the importance of renewable energy and storage for SCE's future.

title: Why this Tesla fan thinks the company is losing its way
summary: An early Tesla adopter and owner of three vehicles criticizes the company for perceived loss of focus on consumer satisfaction, citing numerous product issues and a lack of responsiveness from customer service. Despite his belief in Tesla's mission and Elon Musk's vision, the author, who is now suing the company, fears that poor customer service and faulty design could jeopardize Tesla's future success. He emphasizes that being innovative should not excuse a company from being responsive to its customers.

title: This Week's ETF Launches: The Dow 30 and Russell 1000 Get Alternative Weighting Strategies
summary: This article discusses two new ETFs launched by BlackRock and First Trust that employ alternative weighting strategies for the Russell 1000 and Dow 30, respectively. BlackRock's iShares Russell 1000 Pure U.S. Revenue ETF (AMCA) uses revenue-weighting to focus on U.S.-centric large-cap companies, while First Trust's Dow 30 Equal Weight ETF (EDOW) equally weights components of the Dow Jones Industrial Average to address price-weighting biases. Additionally, WisdomTree updated two of its ETFs (CXSE and XSOE) to include China A-shares in their investable universes.

title: Video Is Coming to Reddit!
summary: Reddit announced the extended rollout of its native video beta, allowing users to capture, upload, and share videos and GIFs directly within the platform. This new feature aims to streamline the content sharing process by removing the need for third-party hosting platforms, making it easier for communities to share rich content and engage in deeper conversations. The beta testing revealed that native video is being used primarily for community-specific engagement rather than personal branding, offering a unique format for expression and interruption-free interaction.

title: Novonix secures Canadian funding for its lithium battery technology
summary: Novonix Limited (ASX:NVX) has secured C$500,000 in funding from the Government of Canada to advance its innovative battery testing technologies. The company, a developer and supplier for the lithium-ion battery industry, will use the funds for research and development of battery chargers and cell testing, aiming to expand its international marketing efforts. This investment is timely as Novonix expects growing demand for energy-efficient batteries, with its expertise already sought by major companies like Apple and Tesla Motors.

title: Cummins Unveils Fully-electric Heavy Duty Truck
summary: Cummins Inc. has unveiled its AEOS Concept Class 7 Urban Hauler EV, a fully electric heavy-duty truck designed with a state-of-the-art battery pack for improved energy-efficiency and density. The truck offers a 100-mile range on a single charge for city driving, extendable to 300 miles with additional battery packs, and incorporates energy-saving technologies like regenerative braking and potential solar panels. This innovation highlights Cummins' commitment to sustainable solutions and zero-emission transportation.

title: LG Group rules out producing its own electric cars
summary: LG Group has clarified that it is not planning to enter the electric vehicle manufacturing business, despite aggressively expanding its presence in the vehicle components sector. An official stated that the company is not considering manufacturing complete vehicles. Industry observers believe LG Group aims to be a comprehensive automotive parts firm, similar to Bosch, rather than an EV manufacturer like Tesla.

title: China’s Electric Car Push Lures Global Auto Giants, Despite Risks (Published 2017)
summary: Global automakers like Volkswagen, General Motors, Renault-Nissan, and Ford are significantly increasing electric car production and research in China, driven by China's heavy investment in infrastructure and pressure on manufacturers. This shift, however, carries a significant risk as China has historically required foreign companies to transfer technology in exchange for market access, a pattern expected to continue with electric vehicle technology. The move is also spurred by new Chinese regulations that will mandate the sale of new-energy cars by automakers in the country.

title: Tesla's head of business development leaves after 11 years
summary: Diarmuid O'Connell, Tesla's vice president of business development, has left the electric car company after more than 11 years. His responsibilities, including government relations, will be taken over by Jon McNeill, president of global sales and service. O'Connell stated he felt it was the right time to move on and spend more time with his family after seeing Tesla grow from a startup through the launch of the Model 3.

title: This is the $50,000 electric pickup truck that will take on Tesla
summary: Workhorse Group is introducing the W-15, an electric pickup truck with a range-extending gas motor, priced at just over $50,000, aiming to compete with Tesla. CEO Stephen Burns highlights its performance claims and notes significant consumer interest, with production for individual consumers set to begin in 2019. The company also anticipates strong demand from fleet users, with initial production vehicles expected in late 2018.

title: Tesla’s China Dream Edges Closer to Reality
summary: China is reportedly considering relaxing rules requiring foreign automakers to have a local partner, a change that could significantly benefit Tesla Inc. This move would allow Tesla to manufacture vehicles in China, a goal the company has pursued due to the country being the world's largest market for electric vehicles. This regulatory shift could address a major hurdle for Tesla, which has struggled to find a suitable local partner.

title: Tesla continues to rack up patents despite Elon Musk’s supposed distaste for patents
summary: Despite Elon Musk's public aversion to patents, Tesla Inc. continues to actively pursue and obtain new patents, including a recent application for a robotic battery swapping system. The article highlights the perceived hypocrisy in Musk's stance, arguing that his companies' patenting activities contradict his claims that patents stifle progress and primarily lead to lawsuits. It suggests that Tesla's ongoing patenting efforts are strategic business decisions, essential for protecting innovations and gaining market advantage, rather than an altruistic move.

title: Tesla is said to shift to Intel from Nvidia for infotainment
summary: Tesla is reportedly switching its infotainment system chip supplier from Nvidia Corp to Intel Corp for its Model 3 and upcoming vehicle versions. This move highlights the growing importance of the automotive market for chipmakers and Intel's strategy to diversify beyond personal computers. While Tesla is a smaller automaker, its adoption of new technology makes such supplier changes significant in the tech industry.

title: Overview of Honda Exhibits at the 45th Tokyo Motor Show 2017
summary: Honda Motor Co., Ltd. announced its lineup of production and concept models for the 45th Tokyo Motor Show 2017, emphasizing the expanding possibilities of people through mobility. The exhibit will feature electrified models like the Honda Sports EV Concept, the all-new Honda CR-V, and celebrate 100 million units of Super Cub production. Honda will also participate in "TOKYO CONNECTED LAB 2017" with concepts promoting family connection.

title: General Motors Is Going All Electric
summary: General Motors announced its commitment to an all-electric, zero-emissions future, planning to introduce 20 new electric models by 2023. This move positions GM among other major automakers embracing electricity, driven by global market demands and environmental regulations, particularly in China. The company aims to make its next generation of electric vehicles profitable through cost reduction and global scale, despite past challenges with electric mobility.

title: Hacking Risk Is What Worries Americans Most About Driverless Vehicles
summary: A survey by American International Group Inc. reveals that U.S. residents are divided on embracing driverless cars, with 42% comfortable and 41% having reservations. The primary concern among those surveyed is the threat of hackers taking control of autonomous vehicles, with 75% expressing this worry. Despite potential benefits like lower insurance premiums, most respondents do not expect widespread adoption of driverless cars within the next two decades.

title: Behind Tesla’s Production Delays: Parts of Model 3 Were Being Made by Hand
summary: Tesla's production of its Model 3 sedan has been significantly hampered by "production bottlenecks," leading to far fewer vehicles than promised. Unknown to most, major parts of the Model 3 were being assembled by hand as recently as early September, away from the automated production line. Experts deem this method highly unusual for mass production, likening it to outdated manufacturing techniques.

title: Tesla Model 3 production falls short of targets in Q3
summary: Tesla Inc. missed its third-quarter production goals for the new Model 3 sedan, delivering only 220 cars and producing a total of 260, far short of CEO Elon Musk's initial projections. The company attributed the shortfall to "production bottlenecks" but stated there are no fundamental issues and expressed confidence in addressing them. This performance raises concerns among analysts about Tesla's ability to transition from a luxury car manufacturer to a mainstream automaker, although the company did report record overall vehicle deliveries for the quarter.

title: GM Buys a Laser Startup to Help It Deliver Your Self-Driving Car, ASAP
summary: General Motors acquired lidar startup Strobe through its self-driving car subsidiary Cruise to significantly reduce the cost of lidar sensors, a critical component for fully driverless vehicles. Strobe's technology is claimed to cut lidar costs by 99 percent and allow the sensor to be collapsed into a single chip, addressing a major bottleneck in the broad deployment of autonomous cars. This acquisition is part of GM's strategy to deploy large fleets of robocars and stay relevant in the evolving automotive future.

title: Tesla Recalling 11,000 Model X SUVs for Seat Issue
summary: Tesla Inc. is recalling 11,000 Model X SUVs globally due to a potential issue where rear seats might not lock into place. The recall affects vehicles manufactured between October 28, 2016, and August 16, 2017, and Tesla estimates only about 3 percent of those have the defect. The company discovered the problem during internal testing and has not received any reports of injuries.

title: Tesla fires hundreds of employees, 400 to 700 may have lost their jobs
summary: Tesla fired hundreds of employees, estimated to be between 400 and 700, as part of its annual performance reviews. This comes as the company is under pressure to ramp up production of its new Model 3 sedan and despite still looking to hire more workers. Tesla denies that union activities played a role in the firings, even though some pro-union employees were among those dismissed.

title: Volvo Unveils a Direct Challenge to Tesla
summary: Volvo has unveiled its first high-performance electric-car model in Shanghai, directly challenging Tesla Inc. This move reinforces Volvo's commitment to exclusively produce electric or hybrid vehicles starting in 2019. Its new stand-alone premium electric-vehicle company, Polestar, will launch its first two vehicles in 2019, backed by a $755 million investment from Volvo and Zhejiang Geely Holding Group Co.

title: Tesla reaches deal to set up a factory in China
summary: Electric-car maker Tesla Inc. has reached an agreement to establish a manufacturing facility in Shanghai, China. This deal, allowing for a wholly-owned factory in the city's free-trade zone, could significantly reduce production costs for Tesla. However, the company would still face China’s 25% import tariff on its vehicles.

title: Elon Musk Was Wrong About Self-Driving Teslas
summary: This article discusses how Elon Musk's promises about Tesla's self-driving capabilities have not materialized as quickly as advertised. Tesla announced a plan for fully autonomous driving a year prior, but the feature is still not fully functional, despite being marketed to customers. The article highlights the discrepancy between the promised self-driving technology and its current implementation.

title: A Tale of Tesla Seats Hints at Why So Few Cars Built
summary: The article explains how Tesla's decision to insource the production of its car seats, driven by Elon Musk's pursuit of perfection and control, is contributing to the company's manufacturing bottlenecks and missed production targets for the Model 3. Industry experts question this vertical integration strategy, suggesting it detracts from Tesla's core competencies and causes production inefficiencies, despite Musk viewing it as an opportunity for innovation. The delays and recalls related to seating highlight the challenges Tesla faces in scaling from a niche luxury producer to a mass-market automaker.

title: Payne: First Tesla Michigan gallery opens at Somerset mall
summary: Tesla Inc. has opened its first stand-alone gallery space in Michigan at the Somerset Collection mall in Troy. This gallery, similar to an Apple store and located next to one, allows customers to learn about Tesla vehicles and energy products but not purchase cars directly due to Michigan's direct-to-consumer sales ban. The opening comes as Tesla battles state laws restricting its direct sales model, showcasing Model S and Model X vehicles, and highlighting its maintenance approach for electric vehicles.

title: SpaceX launches 16th Falcon 9 in 2017, recovers first stage
summary: SpaceX successfully launched its 16th Falcon 9 rocket of 2017, deploying the Koreasat-5A satellite for KT SAT from NASA’s Kennedy Space Center. The mission also achieved a successful recovery of the Falcon 9 first stage aboard the drone ship ‘Of Course I Still Love You,’ marking SpaceX's 19th such recovery. This continued success in first-stage recovery is crucial to SpaceX's long-term strategy for reusable rockets and reducing spaceflight costs.

title: VanEck Long/Flat Trend ETF Historical Data
summary: This article provides historical data for the VanEck Long/Flat Trend ETF (LFEQ) in USD. It includes closing prices, open, high, low, change, and percentage change for various dates, indicating its performance and trading ranges. The ETF's 52-week range and recent daily trading activity are also highlighted.

title: An ETF Is Driven by Electric-Car Batteries
summary: The Global X Lithium & Battery Tech ETF has seen significant growth due to the brightening prospects of a mass market for electric cars. Governments worldwide are implementing regulations to phase out gasoline-powered vehicles, which is expected to drive substantial growth in the electric-car sector, according to Jay Jacobs of Global X Management Co. This trend presents a compelling investment opportunity in the batteries that power these vehicles.

title: Tesla Buys Minnesota-Based Manufacturer
summary: Tesla Inc. has acquired Perbix, a Minnesota-based manufacturer of highly automated equipment that has supplied Tesla for three years. This acquisition is part of CEO Elon Musk's strategy to enhance factory efficiency, following previous acquisitions aimed at boosting manufacturing expertise. Perbix, currently employing 150 people, will remain based north of Minneapolis with plans to recruit more staff.

title: Tencent-backed search firm Sogou jumps 10 percent in U.S. market debut
summary: Sogou Inc.'s shares rose over 10 percent in their U.S. market debut, signaling investor confidence that the Tencent-backed search firm can compete with market leader Baidu. The Beijing-based company's IPO was priced at $13 per American depository share, raising $585 million and valuing the firm at $5.76 billion. Sogou plans to leverage China's massive mobile internet user base to drive revenue through advertising.

title: Lots of talk, little action on remaking Puerto Rico’s grid
summary: Seven weeks after Hurricane Maria, efforts to rebuild Puerto Rico's power grid are chaotic and uncoordinated, with various entities proposing different visions for its future. While some advocate for a cleaner, more resilient system with renewables and microgrids, the U.S. government is mainly focused on restoring the old grid. Authority over the grid's future is divided among several bodies, including PREPA, the Energy Commission, and the Financial Oversight and Management Board, leading to slow progress.

title: First Trust Global Wind Energy ETF ETF Price, Holdings, & News (NYSEARCA:FAN) $FAN
summary: The First Trust Global Wind Energy ETF (FAN) tracks the ISE Global Wind Energy Index, investing at least 90% of its assets in common stocks or depositary receipts of companies in the wind energy sector. The fund has assets under management of $303.17 million and a net expense ratio of 0.60%. Its top holdings include Ørsted A/S, Vestas Wind Systems A/S, and Nordex SE, and it has seen a 21.8% increase in stock price since the beginning of 2026.

title: GM: Next-gen electric cars will cost less, go farther
summary: General Motors announced plans for its next generation of electric vehicles to be 30 percent cheaper than current models, making them profitable after their 2021 debut. CEO Mary Barra expects to reduce battery cell costs to under $100 per kilowatt-hour while achieving a range of over 300 miles. The company is also developing a new manufacturing platform to support multiple brands and segments and aims to roll out 20 new zero-emissions vehicles by 2023.

title: Tesla racial discrimination class action gets 2025 trial date
summary: A California judge has set a tentative pretrial date of August 29, 2025, for a class action lawsuit alleging racial discrimination against nearly 6,000 Black former Tesla workers at its Fremont plant. The class certification aims to establish common facts and determine if injunctive relief is necessary against Tesla, with individual cases to follow for damages. The lawsuit, originally filed in 2017 by Marcus Vaughn, claims Tesla's factory was a "hotbed for racist behavior" and failed to address complaints.

title: Tesla, Elon Musk Unveil Electric Semi-Truck
summary: Tesla Inc. unveiled its all-electric Class 8 tractor, marking its entry into the commercial truck business. The Tesla Semi, slated for 2019 production, is a day cab with a 500-mile range, designed for improved energy efficiency and lower operating costs compared to diesel trucks. It features a unique center driver's seat, dual touchscreens, enhanced autopilot, and advanced safety features, including jack-knife prevention and "armor glass" windshields.

title: New Tesla Roadster upstages rollout of electric big-rig truck
summary: Tesla Inc. CEO Elon Musk unveiled a new $200,000 Roadster, which he claimed would be the fastest production car ever, at an event that was primarily for the debut of an electric heavy-duty truck. The sports car can travel 620 miles on a single charge and accelerate from 0 to 60 mph in 1.9 seconds. This dual unveiling highlighted Tesla's ambitious projects while also drawing attention away from the company's struggles to roll out a more affordable sedan.

title: Trucking company J.B. Hunt reserves Tesla trucks
summary: J.B. Hunt Transport Services Inc. has placed a reservation for Tesla Inc.'s new Semi trucks, following their launch. The trucking company did not specify the exact number of Tesla trucks it plans to acquire. Tesla's Semi trucks aim to compete with traditional diesel trucks by offering an affordable electric alternative with comparable range and cargo capacity.

title: J.B. Hunt, Wal-Mart reserve Tesla electric big rig, analyst questions battery life, cost
summary: J.B. Hunt Transport Services and Wal-Mart Stores have reserved "multiple" Tesla Semi electric big rigs after their unveiling, with J.B. Hunt planning to use them in intermodal and dedicated segments on the West Coast, and Wal-Mart testing 15 trucks in the U.S. and Canada. However, analysts from Jefferies and Stifel are questioning the battery longevity, total cost of ownership compared to diesel, and Tesla's decision to enter a market segment they believe is not well-suited for electric vehicles. Despite Tesla's claims of 500-mile range and lower TCO, concerns remain regarding battery depreciation and the estimated higher upfront cost.

title: J.B. Hunt, Wal-Mart climb aboard Tesla's electric truck
summary: Wal-Mart Stores Inc and J.B. Hunt have placed high-profile orders for Tesla's new electric Semi trucks, though initial plans indicate testing rather than large-volume purchases. Customers are reserving trucks with $5,000 deposits, reflecting uncertainty in the electric commercial vehicle market. Tesla and other manufacturers are investing in electric trucks, anticipating a market shift driven by emissions regulations and government incentives.

title: Tesla unveils ambitious electric semi-truck
summary: Tesla unveiled its new electric semitractor-trailer, with CEO Elon Musk stating it can travel 500 miles on a single charge with a full 80,000-pound load and will be more cost-effective than diesel semis. Production is set to begin in 2019, with a $5,000 deposit required, but the semi's price was not disclosed. The announcement comes amidst Tesla's production struggles with the Model 3 and other ventures.

title: J.B. Hunt Transport Services reserves Tesla electric Class 8 trucks
summary: J.B. Hunt Transport Services announced a reservation to purchase multiple Tesla Semi electric Class 8 trucks, unveiled by Tesla on November 16. The company plans to deploy these electric tractors to its Intermodal and Dedicated Contract Services divisions for West Coast operations, particularly for local and dray routes, aligning with its $500 million investment in technology and sustainable initiatives.

title: Elon Musk’s fast route to more cash: A new Tesla Roadster
summary: Elon Musk surprised attendees at a Tesla event by unveiling a new version of the Roadster, an expensive electric sports car that could quickly generate over $250 million. This comes as Tesla faces a cash drain, and the new Roadster is claimed to be the fastest production car ever. The introduction of the Roadster offers a potential fast route to additional funding for Tesla Inc.

title: Major Fleets Line Up to Test Tesla Semi
summary: Major trucking companies and retailers, including J.B. Hunt, NFI Industries, Wal-Mart, Meijer, and Loblaw Cos., have placed reservations for or plan to test the all-electric Tesla Semi, which is scheduled to enter production in 2019. These companies aim to evaluate the truck's performance in their supply chains, reduce their carbon footprint, and potentially realize cost savings through sustainable technology. While fleets are enthusiastic about the prospect of electric trucks, some key questions remain regarding the economic case, price, and battery pack weight.

title: Retailers to Pilot New Tesla Electric Semi
summary: Several major retailers, including Meijer, J.B. Hunt Transport Services, Inc., and Walmart, are partnering with Tesla to pilot its new electric semi-trucks. These partnerships aim to test the vehicles' performance, reduce carbon footprints, and achieve cost savings through improved fuel efficiency. Production for the semis is expected to begin in 2019, following their unveiling by Elon Musk.

title: Lucid moves its electric car ambitions into a spacious new HQ
summary: Lucid is relocating its headquarters to a new, larger facility in Newark, California, to accommodate growth as it prepares to launch its first vehicle, the Lucid Air. The Lucid Air is an all-electric luxury sport sedan aiming for a 2019 launch, designed to compete with Tesla's Model S, offering high performance and collaborative consumption features. The move signifies a critical phase for Lucid's product development and ambition in the electric vehicle market.

title: Tesla Reveals Price Range for Electric Semi
summary: Tesla Inc. has announced the expected price range for its all-electric Class 8 truck, the Tesla Semi, will be between $150,000 and $200,000. The truck will offer 300 or 500 miles of range and is anticipated to enter production in 2019, with a "founders series" option available for $200,000. Tesla projects significant fuel savings and a two-year payback period for the Semi.

title: The Fuel of Tomorrow: Mining Lithium for Tomorrow’s Cars
summary: This article discusses the crucial role of lithium in the widespread adoption of electric vehicles, highlighting the evolution of EV batteries from lead-acid to the dominance of lithium-ion technology. It emphasizes the increasing demand for lithium and the challenges in its supply, while also showcasing POSCO's innovative lithium extraction technology and its efforts to provide sustainable battery materials.

title: Build fast, fix later: speed hurts quality at Tesla, some workers say
summary: A Reuters investigation, based on accounts from nine current and former Tesla employees, reveals that a significant percentage of Model S and Model X vehicles require fixes after rolling off the assembly line, with some exceeding 90% defect rates. This "build fast, fix later" approach, driven by pressure to maintain production speed, results in costly rework and raises concers about Tesla's ability to scale high-quality manufacturing for its mass-market Model 3. Despite Tesla's claims of rigorous quality control, experts and workers indicate that persistent defects and a lack of manufacturing experience hinder the company's quality standards compared to established luxury automakers.

title: GM: Driverless cars mean big savings for ride-hailing service users
summary: General Motors announced plans to launch a driverless ride-hailing fleet by 2019, expecting it to significantly reduce per-mile costs for consumers, potentially to under $1 by 2025. This strategy aims to make autonomous vehicles profitable for GM, alongside efforts to accelerate consumer acceptance of electric cars through battery development. The company emphasized that removing drivers will increase profitability for fleet operators and generate substantial data through an "Internet of Things" network, positioning GM as a leader in the autonomous and electric vehicle market.

title: Tesla builds world’s largest battery in Australian outback
summary: Tesla has officially plugged in the world's largest lithium-ion battery into Australia's state grid, fulfilling Elon Musk's 100-day guarantee. Located near Jamestown, Australia, the 100-megawatt battery stores energy from the Hornsdale Wind Farm and can power 30,000 homes for up to an hour. This initiative aims to stabilize South Australia's power grid, which has experienced blackouts, and makes the state a leader in dispatchable renewable energy.

title: Tesla Wannabe Lucid Takes on the Auto Industry With an Electric Stunner
summary: Lucid, a Silicon Valley-based electric vehicle startup, is positioning itself as a competitor to Tesla with its luxurious Air sedan. The company emphasizes a pragmatic approach to production, leveraging the experience of former Tesla Model S chief engineer Peter Rawlinson and planning to gradually scale up manufacturing to eventually produce 130,000 cars annually in Casa Grande, Arizona. Lucid aims to capitalize on the growing global demand for electric vehicles, particularly in markets like China that favor large, luxurious sedans.

title: Schwab U.S. TIPS ETF ETF Price, Holdings, & News (NYSEARCA:SCHP)
summary: The Schwab U.S. TIPS ETF (SCHP) invests in U.S. Treasury inflation-protected securities and has seen a 1.2% increase in stock value since the beginning of 2026, trading at $26.80. The fund, managed by Charles Schwab, tracks a market-value weighted index of US Treasury inflation-protected securities with at least one year remaining in maturity. SCHP also declared a monthly distribution of $0.1766 in December 2025 and conducted a 2-for-1 stock split in October 2024.

The article also covers recent news headlines and frequently asked questions about UCC's performance and accessibility.

title: First Trust Emerging Markets AlphaDEX Fund ETF Price, Holdings, & News (NASDAQ:FEM)
summary: The First Trust Emerging Markets AlphaDEX Fund (FEM) is an exchange-traded fund tracking emerging markets companies. Launched in April 2011, it has assets under management of $764.24 million and a dividend yield of 2.56%. The fund's top holdings include Kinsus Interconnect Technology Corp., Unimicron Technology Corp., and Accton Technology Corporation.

title: First Trust Nasdaq Transportation ETF ETF Price, Holdings, & News (NASDAQ:FTXR)
summary: The First Trust Nasdaq Transportation ETF (FTXR) tracks an index of 30 U.S. transportation companies, with major holdings including General Motors, Tesla, and Union Pacific. The ETF has seen its shares increase by 8.8% this year, trading at $42.20 as of February 27, 2026. Institutional investors like Goldman Sachs Group Inc. and Maridea Wealth Management LLC are significant shareholders.

title: Anheuser-Busch Orders 40 Tesla Semi Trucks
summary: Anheuser-Busch has reserved 40 of Tesla Inc.'s all-electric Semi trucks to reduce fuel costs and vehicle emissions. The U.S. subsidiary plans to use these trucks for shipments to wholesalers within a 150 to 200-mile range of its breweries, aligning with Tesla's promised 500-mile range. These vehicles will be integrated into the brewer's dedicated fleets of approximately 750 trucks, which are managed by outside carriers.

title: Traditional Energy is Struggling to Keep Up: General Electric Set to Lay Off 12,000 Workers in 2018
summary: General Electric Co. announced plans to lay off 12,000 workers in 2018 due to decreased demand for fossil fuels as solar and wind energy gain prominence. The company aims to save $1 billion and stabilize its budget, acknowledging the shift in the energy market away from traditional solutions. This decision highlights the challenges faced by established energy companies in adapting to the rapid growth of renewable energy.

title: CEO Mary Barra: GM committed to 'harassment-free' workplace
summary: GM CEO Mary Barra announced the company's commitment to creating a sexual "harassment-free" workplace. She also addressed other key topics including her opposition to repealing the $7,500 federal tax credit for electric vehicles and support for corporate tax reform. Barra additionally discussed GM's progress in autonomous vehicle technology and its strategic decision to sell Opel and Vauxhall businesses in Europe to focus on profitable growth.

title: Industry leaders Rusty Rush & Michael McRoberts of Rush Enterprises talk electric trucks, the growing Tech Rodeo, domestic energy & market conditions
summary: Rusty Rush, head of Rush Truck Centers, and Michael McRoberts discuss the future of electric trucks, anticipating their primary role in the medium-duty, last-mile delivery segment rather than heavy-duty, long-haul trucking. They express skepticism about Tesla's direct sales and service model for commercial vehicles and highlight challenges like infrastructure and payload. The article also touches on the expanding Tech Rodeo, the tech shortage, economic impact on trucking, and the outlook for 2018.

title: PepsiCo makes biggest public pre-order of Tesla Semis: 100 trucks
summary: PepsiCo Inc. has placed the largest known public pre-order for Tesla's electric Semi trucks, reserving 100 vehicles. This move aims to reduce fuel costs and fleet emissions, aligning with PepsiCo's goal to cut greenhouse gas emissions across its supply chain by 20 percent by 2030. The beverage and snack giant plans to use the Semis for shipments between manufacturing facilities, distribution centers, and retailers within the trucks' 500-mile range.

title: Frito-Lay Parent Orders New Tesla Semi Electric Trucks
summary: PepsiCo Inc., the parent company of Frito-Lay, has placed an order for 100 Tesla Semi electric trucks, marking the largest known order for the new long-haul vehicle. The company plans to use these trucks for shipping snack foods and beverages between facilities and to retailers to lower fuel costs and reduce fleet emissions. This move is part of PepsiCo's strategy to cut greenhouse gas emissions by 20 percent across its supply chain.

title: NIO ES8 Challenges the Tesla Model X in China
summary: NIO has launched its first production model, the ES8, an aluminum-bodied, seven-seat electric SUV, in China, positioning it as a competitor to the Tesla Model X. The ES8 features a 70-kWh battery, dual motors producing 644 hp, and advanced automated driving technology including Mobileye's EyeQ4 chip. It also offers a battery swapping service and starts at 448,000 RMB, roughly equivalent to $67,715 USD.

title: Here's What Brown Can Do For Tesla Motors
summary: UPS is purchasing 125 all-electric semi trucks from Tesla, making it the largest known order for the vehicle to date. This move is part of UPS's ongoing efforts to transition towards an electric fleet and reduce fuel expenditures, with plans to thoroughly test the Tesla trucks in real-world routes within the United States. Both companies are collaborating to ensure the success of this "introductory technology" and promote their leadership in green initiatives.

title: Meet the NIO ES8: a Fully Electric, 7-Seat SUV With 220 Miles of Range
summary: Chinese electric carmaker NIO has unveiled its first mass-market model, the ES8 SUV, a 7-seat electric vehicle with an estimated 220 miles of range and standard all-wheel drive, launching in early 2018. It features a swappable battery and is priced at 448,000 Chinese yuan (approx. $68,000 USD), offering a cheaper alternative to the Tesla Model X in China. NIO also announced plans for a second batch of its EP9 hypercar, known for its record-breaking Nürburgring lap time and 1,341 horsepower.

title: Elon Musk Touts Tesla Pickup Plans, Though Light on Detail
summary: Elon Musk has teased plans for a Tesla pickup truck, building on his previous "Master Plan, Part Deux." The Tesla CEO indicated on Twitter that the truck would be released after a new compact SUV, which he suggested could be available as early as 2019. Consistent with his style, Mr. Musk provided few specific details about the new vehicle.

title: All-New Tesla Roadster: What You Need to Know
summary: Tesla unveiled an all-electric second-generation Roadster with record-setting performance figures, including a 0-60 mph sprint in 1.9 seconds and a 620-mile range. The new Roadster, designed by Franz von Holzhausen, features all-wheel drive, a 200 kWh battery, a 2+2 seating configuration, and a removable glass roof. With a base price of $200,000, it aims to outperform existing supercars and will be released in 2020.

title: For Tesla, Deliver, Don’t Promise, in 2018
summary: In 2018, Tesla CEO Elon Musk needs to prioritize the production of the Model 3 mass-market sedan over promising new vehicles like electric semi-trucks or sports cars. Tesla delivered significantly fewer Model 3s than forecasted in the third quarter of 2017, highlighting the need for operational focus. The company's credibility with investors hinges on making its Model 3 dreams a reality and achieving profitable high-volume production.
